content: 1. When co-administering valbenazine with a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor, closely monitor the patient and consider reducing the valbenazine dose based on tolerability. 2. Lorcaserin increases venlafaxine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 3. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and ziprasidone is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 4. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, potentially increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Antipsychotics may enhance serotonergic effects of serotonin modulators, which could result in serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity (e.g., mental status changes, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity) or neuroleptic malignant syndrome (e.g., hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, autonomic dysfunction). 5. Lorcaserin and almotriptan both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Lorcaserin increases amitriptyline levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely. Lorcaserin and amitriptyline both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Lorcaserin increases amoxapine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 8. Lorcaserin and amphetamine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Lorcaserin increases aripiprazole levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and aripiprazole is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 10. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. If also co-administered with a strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Note: In MDD clinical trials, brexpiprazole dosage was not adjusted for strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., paroxetine, fluoxetine); thus, CYP considerations are already factored into general dosing recommendations, and brexpiprazole may be administered without dosage adjustment in patients with MDD. 11. Lorcaserin and bupropion both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Lorcaserin and buspirone both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Lorcaserin increases captopril levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 14. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and cariprazine is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 15. Lorcaserin increases carvedilol levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 16. Lorcaserin increases chloroquine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 17. Lorcaserin increases chlorpromazine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 18. Lorcaserin increases cinacalcet levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 19. Lorcaserin increases citalopram levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and citalopram both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Lorcaserin increases clomipramine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and clomipramine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and clozapine is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 22. Lorcaserin and cocaine topical both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Lorcaserin increases codeine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing the conversion of codeine to its active metabolite morphine. Use caution and monitor the patient. 24. Lorcaserin increases desipramine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and desipramine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Lorcaserin and desvenlafaxine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Lorcaserin increases deuterabenazine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors increase systemic exposure to the active dihydro-metabolites of deuterabenazine by approximately threefold. Do not exceed 18 mg/dose and 36 mg/day of deuterabenazine if co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 27. Lorcaserin and dextroamphetamine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Lorcaserin increases dextroamphetamine transdermal levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Initiate with lower doses and monitor for signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome, particularly during initiation or dosage increase. If serotonin syndrome occurs, discontinue dextroamphetamine transdermal and CYP2D6 inhibitor. 29. Lorcaserin and dextromethorphan both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Lorcaserin increases doxepin levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and doxepin both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Lorcaserin increases doxorubicin levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 32. Lorcaserin increases duloxetine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and duloxetine both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Lorcaserin and eletriptan both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Lorcaserin increases eliglustat levels by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are given concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 35. Lorcaserin increases eluxadoline levels by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 36. Lorcaserin and epinephrine inhaled both increase sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including increased blood pressure and heart rate. Use caution and monitor the patient. 37. Lorcaserin and escitalopram both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Lorcaserin increases flecainide levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 39. Lorcaserin increases fluoxetine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and fluoxetine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Lorcaserin increases fluphenazine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and fluphenazine is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 41. Lorcaserin increases fluvoxamine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and fluvoxamine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lorcaserin and frovatriptan both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Lorcaserin and gepirone both increase serotonin levels. Monitor for symptoms of serotonin syndrome when gepirone is used with other drugs that may affect the serotonergic neurotransmitter systems. If serotonin syndrome occurs, consider discontinuing gepirone and/or concomitant serotonergic drug. 44. Lorcaserin increases haloperidol levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and haloperidol is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 45. Lorcaserin and hydrocodone both increase serotonin levels. Use caution and monitor the patient. 46. Lorcaserin increases iloperidone levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The interaction mechanism between lorcaserin and iloperidone is unspecified. Use caution and monitor the patient. 47. Lorcaserin increases imipramine levels or effects by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorcaserin and imipramine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Lorcaserin decreases the level or effect of iobenguane I 131 by interfering with catecholamine uptake or depleting catecholamine stores, which may reduce iobenguane efficacy. Discontinue interfering drugs for at least five half-lives before administration of either the dosimetry or an iobenguane dose. Do not administer these drugs until at least seven days after each iobenguane dose.
